script.opening_words: Have you ever stared at your bank account showing $100,000 and wondered if you're actually rich or just really good at pretending to be? Most people think hitting six figures means they've made it. But here's the uncomfortable truth that your high school math teacher conveniently forgot to mention. That $100,000 sitting in your account isn't the finish line. It's actually the starting gun for a race you didn't even know you were running. My name is Nick and I
script.ending_words: $100,000 isn't just sitting there looking pretty in your account. It's actually the financial equivalent of being pregnant with twins when you thought you were just getting a little chunky. Uh, the math doesn't lie. Even when it seems too good to be true, time and compound interest are working in your favor, but only if you stop making excuses and actually give them the chance to do their job.
script.analysis: Full 19758 canonical characters read. A compound-interest walkthrough: hook ($100K is the starting gun); linear-thinking strawman; eighth-wonder line; $500/month at 8% milestones (12 years to $100K, 6 more to $200K, "20 years", 35 years to $1M, 40 years to $2M); inflation and crashes objections (8% "inflation-adjusted"); budget cuts (food $700, car $800); psychology of a six-figure balance; options and opportunities; rising contributions; culture of instant gratification; employer match; close (pregnant-with-twins line). Verified: 35-year $1.15M from $210K. Wrong: $100K takes 10.6 years and the contribution/returns split ($84K/$16K) is wrong; "20 years at $200K" (actually $294,510); year-40 "over $2M" ($1.75M) and "$160K a year" ($140K); car payment "over $800" (Edmunds ~$754 new). Contradiction: 8% called both conservative and inflation-adjusted. The stored ending is complete.
beat_map: Six more years to $200K; "20 years in".

claim_audit.assessment: [INDEPENDENT_CALCULATION_VERIFIED] Monthly compounding at 8%/12: $100,000 is reached after 10.6 years (127.6 months); after 12 years the balance is $120,254. Contributions at $100,000 are ~$64,000 (12 years = $72,000); $84,000 corresponds to 14 years. Returns at $100,000 are ~$36,000, not $16,000. The split is wrong.
